text:
Say. The whole square stays fixed. Teal names the two columns; coral names the three rows. Gold is the overlap.
Ask. Why does the denominator become twelve?
Expect. Three equal columns crossed by four equal rows produce twelve equal parts; six are in both groups.
If stuck. Count the rows and columns before counting gold parts.
Time. 4 minutes, followed by a student explanation.

Say. Cut the left triangle and translate it to the right. No area is added or removed.
Ask. Why is the slanted side not the height?
Expect. The height is perpendicular to the six-centimeter base.
If stuck. Trace the marked right angle.
Time. 5 minutes, including a sketch and explanation.

Say. Today we connect the picture of a part of a part to its calculation.
Ask. What could the gold overlap represent?
Expect. A conjecture about two thirds of three fourths.
If stuck. Name each shading separately.
Time. 2 minutes.
